subsystems.name: Cryptographic inventory
subsystems.role: find every place encryption, hashing and signing are used, including the ones nobody documented.

subsystems.name: Data lifetime classification
subsystems.role: work out which secrets must stay confidential for longer than a quantum computer is likely to take to arrive.

subsystems.name: Crypto-agility layer
subsystems.role: lets algorithms be swapped out without rewriting every system.

subsystems.name: Post-quantum key establishment
subsystems.role: replaces RSA and elliptic-curve key exchange — the part of a session that captured traffic exposes first.

subsystems.name: Post-quantum authentication
subsystems.role: signatures and certificates a future quantum computer cannot forge.

subsystems.name: Key management and hardware roots
subsystems.role: store, rotate and retire the new keys.
parts: HSMs and secure elements with PQC support

buildSteps.title: Inventory and classify
buildSteps.detail: Discover everywhere RSA or elliptic-curve cryptography is used, then mark each secret with how many years it must stay confidential.

buildSteps.title: Rank by exposure
buildSteps.detail: Anything whose secrecy must outlast the expected arrival of a quantum computer is urgent; short-lived session data is not.

buildSteps.title: Build crypto-agility first
buildSteps.detail: Expose algorithm choices as configuration rather than hard-coded constants, so the next migration is a rollout, not a rewrite.

buildSteps.title: Deploy hybrid key exchange
buildSteps.detail: Turn on ML-KEM alongside X25519 in TLS and VPNs, so traffic is protected even if one of the two algorithms is later broken.

buildSteps.title: Retire static key exchange
buildSteps.detail: Move off static RSA and static elliptic-curve key exchange, where one long-term private key unlocks years of recorded sessions.

buildSteps.title: Migrate signatures and firmware
buildSteps.detail: Move certificates, code signing and secure boot to post-quantum algorithms — including hash-based signatures for devices that can never be updated again.

buildSteps.title: Rotate long-lived secrets
buildSteps.detail: Re-key and re-encrypt stored data, rotate credentials and tokens, and shorten certificate lifetimes so already-recorded ciphertext loses value.

buildSteps.title: Govern and decommission
buildSteps.detail: Publish deadlines, track which systems still allow quantum-vulnerable algorithms, and switch them off rather than leaving them as a fallback.

prerequisites.why: ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA were published as NIST Federal Information Processing Standards in 2024.
many embedded and industrial devices have algorithms baked into silicon and cannot be changed later.
keys must live in tamper-resistant hardware, and HSM support for larger post-quantum keys is still arriving.
post-quantum public keys and signatures are far larger, straining constrained devices and certificate chains.
the risk exists before the machine does — that is the whole point of harvesting traffic now.

pathway.milestone: standards published and hybrid post-quantum key exchange running in mainstream browsers and TLS
pathway.unlocks: recorded traffic that can no longer be broken by a future quantum computer.

pathway.milestone: post-quantum certificates, code signing and firmware in operational systems
pathway.unlocks: authentication that survives a quantum attack, not just confidentiality.

pathway.milestone: regulated and national-security systems phase out RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography by the early 2030s
pathway.unlocks: a hard deadline that forces legacy systems to be rebuilt or retired.
data encrypted today still secret when a large-scale quantum computer eventually exists.
